heading: 4.3 Objective Three: combined-test accuracy in children and adults
objective: To compare the diagnostic performance of MAS and hs-CRP and MAS or hs-CRP in children younger than 16 years and adults aged 16 years and above.
methods: Histopathology was the reference standard: acute, suppurative, phlegmonous, gangrenous and perforated appendicitis were positive; reactive lymphoid hyperplasia was negative. Simple appendicitis comprised the first three positive categories and complicated appendicitis comprised gangrenous or perforated disease. MAS ≥7 and hs-CRP >3 mg/L were positive. “MAS and hs-CRP” required both tests to be positive; “MAS or hs-CRP” required either test to be positive. Neither combination was designated the single prespecified primary rule. The corrected hs-CRP threshold is >3 mg/L throughout this report. Both rules were recalculated from participant records; no missing values were excluded. There were 19 children (18 reference-positive, one negative) and 66 adults (59 positive, seven negative). Wilson intervals describe proportions. Independent age-group contrasts use two-sided Fisher exact tests, conservative ≥95% difference intervals from simultaneous 97.5% exact bounds and Holm adjustment across six tests.
finalParagraph: At the corrected >3 mg/L hs-CRP threshold, both combination rules showed broadly similar observed sensitivities across ages, and no adjusted age contrast was established. Specificity in children remains highly uncertain. These fixed rules do not define a continuous combined score, so conventional combined ROC curves, fitted-model bootstrap refitting and leave-one-out validation are not applicable.
